## What actually ran

Everything below was measured on-box on 2026-08-13, Windows 11, llama.cpp
**b10375 (ba360efe1)**, both servers launched detached with `-lv 4` and stderr
redirected to `traces/logs/{root,leaf}-server.log`:

- **leaf** — `tools/llamacpp-rocm/llama-server.exe`, `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M`,
  `-c 327680 -np 8 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on -ub 512 -b 2048 -lm none
  --no-kv-unified --cont-batching -lv 4`, env `ROCBLAS_USE_HIPBLASLT=1`.
  Launch log: 41/41 layers offloaded to ROCm0, KV 3400 MiB (40960 cells, 10
  layers, 8/8 seqs), K/V q8_0, flash_attn enabled.
- **root** — `tools/llamacpp-vulkan/llama-server.exe`, `Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M`,
  `-c 32768 -np 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on -ub 512 -b 2048 -lm none
  --no-context-shift -lv 4`. 65/65 layers offloaded to Vulkan0, KV 1088 MiB
  (32768 cells, 16 layers, 1/1 seqs), K/V q8_0, flash_attn enabled.
- `uv run --python 3.12 -m rlm.cli validate --config config.yaml` → exit 0
  (config, prompt registry, both `/props` probes, both KV-cache-type
  assertions from the launch logs, AppContainer confinement probe) — *after*
  finding F1 below.
- `-lm none` is b10375's spelling of §4's `--no-mmap` (R11 flag drift);
  `config.yaml`'s `extra_flags` were updated to match what actually launched.

## Findings

### F1 — `rlm validate` refused every correctly-launched server (fixed)

`rlm.cli._BUILD_LINE` required a separator (`build:` / `build =`). b10375
prints `common_params_print_info: build 10375 (ba360efe1) with Clang 20.1.8`,
with **no separator**, so `parse_launch_log` recovered no build id,
`log_is_current` returned False, and `validate` refused both servers as
`UNVERIFIED` — a gate failing closed on servers that were in fact exactly what
config said they were. This regex had never met a real server: it was written
from the older upstream shape. Fixed (separator optional) and pinned by a new
test carrying the verbatim live lines. **`/props` reports `b10375-ba360efe1`,
not `10375 (ba360efe1)`** — the substring cross-check in `log_is_current`
survives that difference by luck, not design, and is now covered by the test.

### F2 — a test that silently inverted once real servers existed (fixed)

`tests/conftest.py::valid_config_file` redirected the trace paths into
`tmp_path` but inherited the shipped config's **relative** `log_path`. With the
S1 servers running, `traces/logs/*-server.log` existed and were current, so
`test_validate_refuses_when_the_cache_type_is_unverified` — whose entire
premise is that no launch log exists — passed validation and failed. Fixed by
redirecting `log_path` into `tmp_path` too. The suite was green at 163 tests
precisely because no real server had ever run beside it.

### F3 — leaf calls bypass the chat template (NOT fixed; the headline finding)

`LLMDispatcher.query` POSTs the root's composed string straight to
`/completion`. Nothing applies `/apply-template` for the leaf role, and nothing
prepends the registry's `leaf_prefix`. Against a real instruct model that is
base-model prompting, and it shows: **every leaf answer in this gate was junk.**
All seven in-episode leaf calls returned either `''` or
`'\n\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\nNONE'` — the model's own pre-closed think block
leaking into a string the root then treats as data (an R5/R12 surface the spec
does not currently name). The two leaf probes returned prompt echo:
`'\n\nREF-36862762 / f7fc\n\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\nREF-36862762 / f7fc'`.

Diagnosed, not guessed. Same prompt, same server, same sampling:

| leaf call shape | result |
|---|---|
| raw prompt → `/completion` (what the scaffold does) | echoes the trailing instruction 3×, emits `<think></think>`, then `NONE` |
| `/apply-template` (`enable_thinking=false`) → `/completion` | clean `NONE` — right format, still wrong answer (see F4) |
| `/apply-template` (`enable_thinking=true`) → `/completion` | reasons for 512 tokens and never reaches an answer |

The byte-identical leaf prefix is scheduled for S2 (§9 S2). The **template**
omission is not scheduled anywhere, and it degrades every leaf call from S1
onward. It also means the leaf has no `enable_thinking` control at all:
`scaffold.root.enable_thinking` exists, its leaf counterpart does not.

### F4 — the leaf cannot extract at chunk scale on this corpus

With the template applied by hand (so F3 is not the cause), the same needle:

| haystack | thinking off | thinking on (n_predict 2048) |
|---|---|---|
| 574 tokens | **found** | **found** |
| ~9,850 tokens | `NONE` | `NONE` (reasons: "no syndicate names") |
| ~31,500 tokens | `REF-56850 / a4bc` (wrong id — a confabulation) | `NONE` |

**Stated caveat:** this filler is deliberately uniform pseudo-random word
salad, a harder haystack than natural prose — one distinctive paragraph among
~300 structurally identical ones, with no semantic anchors. So this bounds leaf
reliability on adversarially-uniform text, not on real corpora. Even so it
lands directly on the §7 #2 chunk-size sweep: **chunk size now has a quality
axis, not only a throughput one**, and 32,768 may be above this leaf's usable
extraction range. S2's leaf-envelope and evidence-span work should measure
extraction accuracy against chunk size before the benchmark is frozen.

### F5 — the gate passed *without* the leaf. Both fixtures were solved in code

Five of twelve episodes made **zero** leaf calls; the other seven made exactly
one, got the junk above, and **recovered by falling back to the REPL**. The
paraphrase fixture — designed so a regex for the answer cannot find it, and
intended to force ≥1 useful leaf call — was solved every time by the root
locating the register in code and printing two windows around it. Trace
`7447a4be…` is the canonical example: keyword scan → one leaf call → `NONE` →
"The sub-model returned NONE. Let me first look at what's in chunk 1" →
`re.finditer` → `chunk1[idx:idx+500]` → answer.

That is the scaffold behaving exactly as §5's tips and the `needle` strategy
template prescribe (scan in code, treat sub-answers as untrusted). It is also
the honest reading of this gate: **arm (b)'s 3/3 is attributable to the
root + REPL path alone.** The leaf path is, as of S1, unproven — F3 must be
fixed and the S2 fixtures must re-test it before any benchmark claim rests on
sub-calls.

### F6 — the evidence-span check is inert as the prompt uses it

`prompts/strat-needle.v1.md` step 5 tells the root to verify the span before
submitting. In `f2e7c554…` and `7447a4be…` the root put `verifies(...)` and
`final_answer(...)` in the **same cell** — so the check printed
`Verifies: False` (correct: the paraphrase answer is by construction not a
verbatim span) *after* the answer had already been submitted. The answer was
right, so the episode passed on the checker; the guard did nothing. A check the
model can and does run after the irreversible action is not a guard. S2's
scaffold-side envelope (§9 S2) is the right home for this; noting it here so it
is not rediscovered as a benchmark anomaly.

### F7 — the control arm refuses rather than confabulates (R5, positive)

All six control attempts answered `NOT PRESENT` in 4 tokens. The 27B root did
not invent a UUID or a name when the fact was outside its window. The control
is therefore 0/3 for the right reason (the needle is genuinely absent), not
because the model produced garbage that happened to miss the checker.

### F8 — prefix caching works across episodes (R3/§7 #3b, positive)

Leaf `tokens_cached` was 29,067–29,207 on every call after the first for a
given fixture — i.e. an entire 29.5K-token chunk prefill reused **across
process boundaries**, since each episode ran in its own `uv run`. Root
`cache_prompt` reuse is equally visible in arm (a): 133.6 s for the first
28K-token control attempt, **3.6 s** for the next two.

## R1 checkpoint: the A/B has no resolving power on these fixtures

6/6 vs 6/6 is a ceiling tie, not a result. The S1 fixtures do not discriminate
between the two root prompts, so nothing was learned about worked exemplars
beyond their cost (+1,203 root prompt tokens per episode, 1,664 → 2,867 on turn
1). Per the pre-registered rule the tie breaks to the simpler prompt: **`v1`
stays pinned**, sha256
`1c58a5813e7d62cf2721843b01106b2e59cb5734b95a38e660f81229fad6f24f`, recorded in
`config.yaml` with the reason. The A/B is closed at two variants (§9 S1 hard
cap) and nothing was tuned in response to results.

What R1 (root degrades under the scaffold) actually got tested against here:
the root wrote correct, purposeful Python in 55 turns across 12 episodes with
zero cell-extraction misses, zero budget breaches, zero errors, and a max reply
of 388 tokens. On this evidence the 27B root is not degrading inside the
scaffold — but the tasks were solved by code, and the harder question (does it
degrade when it must *orchestrate sub-calls*) is untestable until F3 is fixed.

## Re-derived leaf `max_predict` — refused, with the number stated

Observed leaf answer lengths were `[1, 1, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 31, 35]` (n=9, median
7, max 35). Taken at face value that argues for `max_predict.leaf` ≈ 64. **It
is not taken at face value:** every one of those samples came from the
untemplated leaf path (F3), so the distribution describes a defect, not a
workload. `max_predict.leaf` stays at **512**, and the re-derivation is
deferred to S2, when leaf calls will carry a chat template and the S2 fixtures
will exercise real extraction. The root side *is* usable and confirms its
default: 55 root turns, max 388 tokens out, `max_predict.root` 1024 unchanged.

## Scaffold behaviour against real models — the parts that held

- 12/12 episodes reached `final_answer`; **no** budget breach, wall-clock kill,
  context exhaustion, sandbox death, dispatcher error, or retry.
- Cell extraction: 55 root turns, **zero** extraction misses (`status=rejected`
  never appeared).
- `rlm replay 7447a4be… --online` → all four checks green: 6 root turns
  rehashed offline, prompt hashes matched, 6-turn message array re-derived from
  the trace alone, and byte-equal `/apply-template` re-render against the live
  server. The §6 state rule holds on real traffic, not just fakes.
- Per-episode wall clock 51–150 s (mean 108 s) — far inside the 900 s budget,
  so C5's `max_wall_clock` was never the binding constraint at this corpus size.

## Verdict

**S1 GATE: PASS**, on the terms §9 states: control 0/3, RLM 3/3 with the pinned
prompt, on a ≥64K-token synthetic needle the control provably cannot see.

It is a qualified pass and should be recorded as one. The scaffold's *loop* is
proven — sandbox, chunker, root turn cycle, final-answer channel, budgets,
trace, replay. Its *delegation* is not: the leaf path is broken at the
transport layer (F3), and every episode that touched it recovered by ignoring
it. S2 must not be started on the assumption that sub-calls work; F3 is the
first thing to fix, and F4 says the chunk-size sweep needs a quality axis when
it does.
